caption: Nagare, private token vesting on Starknet
narrate: Nagare is private token vesting on Starknet. A sender funds a lockup, the recipient withdraws what has vested, and no wallet address of either party appears in any Nagare transaction.

block.tag: Live on mainnet  ·  STRK20 anonymizer  ·  no owner, no upgrade path

caption: Every other vesting contract names both parties in public
narrate: Every other vesting contract names both parties in public. Open a Tokei or Sablier stream on a block explorer and you can read the cap table straight off it, and that record does not expire.

block.title: Every other vesting contract names both parties in public.

caption: The Nagare app
narrate: Nagare moves the funding and the payouts through the S T R K twenty pool. The sender and the recipient of a schedule are Stark curve keys generated in the browser, so neither wallet ever appears next to the other.

caption: What the chain can see
narrate: The design hides the parties and publishes the terms. The wallet that funded a schedule, the wallet that receives it, and the wallet behind any payout are never published. Every amount, every date and every key is.

caption: Opening a schedule
narrate: Opening a schedule takes an amount, a cliff and an end date. It can be cancellable, or you can switch that off, and Nagare records a sender key that has no private key behind it, so nobody can cancel it afterwards, the sender included. Funding it is one signature in your wallet.

caption: Schedule 3 on mainnet
narrate: This is schedule three on mainnet. It was funded, the sender cancelled it, and the recipient withdrew the part that had vested. Anyone can read those amounts and dates. What the contract stores for each side is a public key, and no address of either party appears in any transaction on this schedule.

caption: The same activity on a block explorer
narrate: Here is the pool paying the Nagare contract to fund a schedule. Starkscan reads it as a privacy pool withdrawal, one S T R K out of the pool, and the explorer states that the public trail ends there, because nothing on chain connects it to the deposit that funded it.

caption: What Nagare does not claim
narrate: The claim is narrow, and worth stating exactly. Shielding is public. Amounts and timing can be correlated. The contract has no owner and no upgrade path, and it has not been audited.
